name: The DPRK Remote Worker Threat: Unmasking North Korea's Digital Deception

attribution.legal_posture: Publisher-attributed public research finding; legal adjudication and civil identity require separate evidence.

caveats: Keep raw IPs, exposed services, and victim infrastructure out of publication.
Tool presence is one contextual signal. Correlate identity, interview, endpoint, shipping and access signals.

statements: Flashpoint describes parallel personas, virtual-camera software, remote-management tools and IP-KVM devices as a combined means of passing interviews and controlling employer systems.
The report says supervisors may use workforce-monitoring software such as Classroom Spy Pro and simple LAN messaging to supervise teams, supporting an internal-control/digital-work-farm TTP.

Recommended detections include newly created cookie-cutter GitHub profiles, sparse LinkedIn networks with suspicious mutual connections, public-VPN or impossible-location logins, unauthorized remote tools and repeated equipment shipping destinations.
